generation.prompt:
Create one photorealistic vertical 9:16 educational photograph of Recycling sorting centre (回收分拣中心). The result must look like a single candid real-world photograph, never a collage, cutaway diagram, catalogue layout or labelled illustration.

SCENE DIRECTION
Photograph an orderly materials-recovery facility from a protected visitor walkway, looking down slightly onto one stopped sorting conveyor. Place a single clear plastic bottle and crushed aluminium can in separate foreground sections of the belt, with the magnetic separator visible above. Show the blue recycling container and glass hopper on opposite sides, a compressed cardboard bale and tied paper bundle behind them, and the bale-clamp attachment on a parked forklift at the rear. Hang one pair of protective gloves at the empty sorting station. Use bright industrial skylight and muted machinery colours so the materials read clearly. No workers reaching into equipment, loose glass shards, readable packaging, mountains of rubbish, dirty haze, duplicated containers or active dangerous machinery.

REQUIRED LEARNING TARGETS
Show exactly one clear primary instance of each of these ten targets: materials-sorting conveyor, blue recycling container, compressed cardboard bale, crushed aluminium drink can, clear recyclable plastic bottle, overhead magnetic separator, protective sorting gloves, glass collection hopper, forklift bale-clamp attachment, recycled paper bundle.

COMPOSITION AND LEGIBILITY
Distribute the targets across the upper, middle and lower thirds and across both sides of the portrait frame. Preserve realistic scale, perspective, contact shadows and spatial relationships. Every target must have a distinct silhouette, be large enough to identify on a phone screen, and remain fully visible rather than hidden behind a person, furniture or another target. People may perform natural actions, but their hands and bodies must not cover the learning targets. Keep incidental background objects visually quiet.

STRICT EXCLUSIONS
No captions, vocabulary labels, subtitles, watermarks, brand logos, readable signage, licence-plate text or gibberish lettering. No duplicated target objects, floating objects, malformed hands, extra limbs, distorted tools, impossible reflections or physically incoherent architecture.
